title: I Posted the Podcast-Booth Hours After They Camped My Numbered Interface

parts.text: I stepped into booth C at 3:04 p.m. and host Rae was already using my numbered interface. The board said: FIFTY MINUTES. INTERFACES STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-five, studio intern, holding a clipboard that listed our session. Rae shrugged. "Hosts are the booth." I photographed the board, the booking, and her cables on my interface. Then I asked for the booth hours. At 3:12 the studio desk pinged why Rae's cables sat on our interface. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio desk can see Rae's cables in booth C during our session.

social.video_title: She camped my numbered podcast interface — Part 1/2
social.description: Podcast booth, a host on my interface, a fifty-minute clock she posted. I logged the cables. Would you have asked for the booth hours?

parts.text: Rae called it levels until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the interface still. The interface went back to my numbered bag. Rae ran a slot of their own and told the next host atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: HOSTS ARE NOT THE BOOTH. I keep our session on a labeled card. Rae brown-bags her cables. The booth finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Hosts are not the booth — Part 2/2
social.description: Booth hours, numbered interface, and a second line on the board. Were levels ever our session?
